name: Mark Kelly
role: U.S. Senator from Arizona (Democratic, since December 2020); retired U.S. Navy captain and NASA astronaut
summary: Mark Kelly is a Democratic senator from Arizona who ran as a bipartisan moderate and favours abortion rights, same-sex marriage, a higher minimum wage, union organizing, background checks and a public health-insurance option. He backs a strong military and traditional alliances, support for Ukraine, nuclear power and an all-of-the-above energy policy, opposes most Trump tariffs, and has combined border-security measures with a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers. In 2025-26 he became a leading critic of the Trump administration after appearing in a video telling service members they may refuse illegal orders, which led to a Pentagon investigation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 2020 campaign site says he believes health care is a right and supports ensuring every Arizonan has insurance, with a public option competing with private insurers; he said he was unsure about single-payer and did not want employer coverage to end, and Wikipedia reports he opposes Medicare for All. Position is a guaranteed-coverage public-option model, not a fully state-run system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In April 2025 he joined the Raise the Wage Act raising the federal minimum from $7.25 to $17 and said 'It's past time we do right by workers and raise the minimum wage'; he also voted for a $15 amendment in 2021.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His campaign page backs ending the tax breaks for the super wealthy and big corporations, and in 2025 he criticised 'huge tax breaks to rich people'. He has not stated a specific rate increase.

unions-good.rationale: Backing the PRO Act in March 2025 he said 'I grew up in a union household and it was my mom getting a good union job that really changed things for our family' and that he supports workers' right to organize.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Repeatedly calls for tougher oversight of specific industries: 'When corporations take advantage of a crisis – that's price gouging. And it's wrong' and he is 'leading the fight to hold companies accountable'; his platform backs more oversight of hospital costs and taking on drug companies.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No recorded position on recreational drugs generally; in 2020 he said he would probably vote yes on Arizona's marijuana initiative, which covers marijuana only.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun owner and 'strong supporter of the 2nd Amendment' who backs universal background checks, red flag laws and says laws are too lax; he did not call for strict limits on ownership in the sources found, so the evidence is moderate regulation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: After the Senate passed the Respect for Marriage Act he said 'marriage equality is a fundamental right' and 'I am proud to have voted for marriage equality'.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted to advance the Women's Health Protection Act to write Roe v. Wade into law, saying 'I'm going to vote to make sure that women can make these decisions for themselves'; his site says he 'supports every woman's right to choose'.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Called for accountability on deep systemic racism and for addressing racial justice issues threatening Black lives.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No recorded position on the overall level of immigration.

free-trade.rationale: Opposes broad tariffs as a tax on importers and consumers that disrupts supply chains; does not argue for protectionism.

nation-first.rationale: Platform stresses working with allies and partners to tackle shared threats and restoring US leadership through traditional alliances, which points against putting national interest ahead of global cooperation.

open-borders.rationale: Said in February 2020 'I'm completely on the record – I'm not for open borders. I think we need border security'; his platform calls for a strong, secure border.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Says 'we've got to get off fossil fuels' and backs massive public investment in renewables and the Inflation Reduction Act, but said he is 'not in favor of the Green New Deal', so support for large but not drastic action.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Cosponsored the ADVANCE Act (2023) and leads bills with Sen. Lummis to ease nuclear permitting, construction costs and uranium enrichment licensing, and chaired a May 2026 hearing on them.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Opposes Trump's tariffs: 'These are taxes on working families and businesses' and called the tomato tariffs a 'billion-dollar tax' that will not solve the problems of American growers. This is opposition to specific tariffs, not a stated view on protective tariffs in general.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Was a chief negotiator of the CHIPS and Science Act, a federal industrial investment in domestic microchip production.

political-violence-never.rationale: Responding to the Kirk killing he said 'I feel like this is un-American', and has repeatedly condemned political violence, citing his wife's shooting; no sentence stating that it is never justified was found.

military-superiority.rationale: Said the 2022 defense bill would help 'maintain our competitive edge over China' and that 'we will continue to be the best military in the world'.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Co-introduced bills that secured water rights and land for several Arizona tribes, signed in January 2023.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said 'I will always support Israel's right to exist as a successful and prosperous nation' and wants 'a future where the Jewish state of Israel is secure', while criticising Netanyahu's government and voting for resolutions blocking some arms transfers in April 2026.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted for the $900 billion COVID relief law and the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan and backed federal aid to states; he also criticised tax breaks that explode the national debt, so evidence leans against avoiding deficit stimulus but is not a stated view on the principle.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: In 2022 he said 'we currently need an all-of-the-above strategy that includes increased domestic production of crude oil' and with Sen. Manchin urged more Gulf of Mexico oil and gas leasing; he did not address coal and also backs renewables.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says Dreamers are as American as anyone and supports equal rights for LGBTQ people, including marriage.

separated-powers.rationale: Backed war powers resolutions to let Congress check the president on the Iran war.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Platform says he is 'committed to rebuilding our traditional alliances and restoring American leadership' and he describes 'the coalition that we lead' in support of Ukraine.

ban-cartels.rationale: His office credits him with pushing the administration to address anti-competitive practices in meatpacking; no broader statement on breaking up concentrations of economic power.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: His platform says he 'opposes legislation weakening Social Security or efforts to gamble seniors' retirement security in the stock market' and opposes plans to privatise it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Co-leads the Ban Corporate PACs Act and said 'big corporations have too much sway on what happens in Washington'; he refuses corporate PAC money.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Original cosponsor of the Equality Act, which bars discrimination on gender identity, and said he supports it so that every Arizonan can live 'free from any discrimination'. His own words do not address legal recognition of gender identity specifically.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Navy combat veteran whose platform says he 'understands the importance of a strong military' and who works on the defence bill as an Armed Services member.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Argues the US should work with allies against Russia and China: Putin must be defeated and 'China is watching... the strength of the coalition that we lead'.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said 'too much money and power is concentrated in the hands of a few rich people and corporations' and that big corporations have too much sway in Washington; he did not use the language of liberty explicitly.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: In June 2020 he said 'I do not agree that we should defund the police' and favored reforming policing; he did not address prisons.

future-generations.rationale: On Earth Day 2020 he said Arizona's treasures must be protected for future generations and 'we have an obligation to continue working to protect and preserve our environment'.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Wants students to avoid 'crushing debt' through fully funded Pell Grants and lower federal loan interest rates; he did not call for cancelling loans in the sources found.

voter-id.rationale: Opposes the 2026 SAVE America Act, which requires documentary proof of citizenship to register, saying it is 'not about voter ID' and that driver's licences should be enough; he did not state a general position on ID requirements.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Calls for accountability on deep systemic issues with racism, which points against the claim that racism is no longer the main obstacle.

notes:
Wikipedia and Senate pages show he is alive and the sitting senator (term to 2029). Positions come mainly from his 2020 campaign pages, Senate press releases and floor remarks, so some older campaign positions may have shifted: he declined in 2020 to take a position on the filibuster but in 2022 said he would back a majority-vote change for voting-rights bills (no statement in the test covers this). Many answers are null because no statement of his speaks to them; his wife Gabby Giffords' positions were not used. His 2026 break with Israel arms transfers is noted under jewish-state-israel, which concerns Israel's right to exist, not arms policy.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 7 answers taken from it, 15 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Evidence is thin on labor, Ukraine (2022 statements could not be opened), China, technology and marijuana: kelly.senate.gov, markkelly.com, congress.gov, Vote Smart and the 2020/2022 debate transcripts returned 403 or no transcript, so those themes rely on news reports and dated quotes from compilations. Many answers are null because no opened source addressed the statement. Kelly's 2026 AI proposal (Make AI Work for Americans Act) was not mapped to any statement. His 2020 Vote Smart questionnaire answers could not be read.
